proposals.note: Designed a translationally invariant ansatz block on a ring topology. The block consists of two entangling layers separated by a parameterized rotation layer. All single-qubit rotations within a layer share the same trainable parameter (p0 for the first layer, p1 for the second), and the entangling layers use a uniform nearest-neighbor CNOT ring (0-1-2-3-4-5-0). This structure enforces cyclic symmetry (invariance under the generator [1,2,3,4,5,0]), which aligns with the periodic nature of the input domain [0, 2*pi) and the site indexing. This symmetry constraint reduces the parameter space dimensionality significantly compared to prior proposals (2 params vs 4), potentially improving generalization and reducing overfitting risk while maintaining sufficient expressivity through the repeated layers and feature map re-uploading.

proposals.note: Designed a 6-parameter block with translational symmetry on a ring topology. The block consists of local rotations (RZ, RY) followed by a cyclic CNOT ladder. Parameters are tied by site index (p_i applied to wire i), enforcing a translation-invariant structure across the 6 sites. This reduces parameter count from 12 (in c0004) to 6 while maintaining sufficient entanglement depth (2 layers of CNOTs) and local expressivity. The structure is designed to capture periodic features in the input vector x_0..x_5, leveraging the assumption that the underlying function may have shift-invariant properties or that the feature map re-uploads data in a way that benefits from shared weights across sites.

proposals.note: Designed a dense entangling block with 16 trainable parameters to maximize expressivity within the 24-gate limit. The structure uses a linear CNOT chain (0-1-2-3-4-5) followed by a wrap-around (5-0) and a second pass (0-1-1-2) to ensure strong connectivity across all 6 qubits. Each qubit receives RY and RZ rotations before entanglement, providing full single-qubit control. This high-parameter count (16) contrasts with prior low-parameter proposals, aiming to better fit the complex analytic targets alpha_0 and alpha_1 by leveraging the full capacity of the ansatz block.
